simple.meaning: פַּתְבַּג (pathbag) is a Hebrew word meaning “a dainty.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פַּתְבַּג (H6598) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 1:5, with occurrences in Daniel.

simple.summary: פַּתְבַּג (pathbag) / H6598 is traced through Daniel 1:5, Daniel 1:8, Daniel 1:13, Daniel 1:15 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king appointed for them a daily portion of the king’s dainties, and of the wine which he drank, and that they should be nourished three years; that at its end they should stand before the king.

timeline.evidenceText: The king appointed for them a daily portion of the king’s dainties, and of the wine which he drank, and that they should be nourished three years; that at its end they should stand before the king.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s dainties, nor with the wine which he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Then let our faces be examined before you, and the face of the youths who eat of the king’s dainties; and as you see, deal with your servants.”
At the end of ten days, their faces appeared fairer, and they were fatter in flesh, than all the youths who ate of the king’s dainties.
So the steward took away their dainties, and the wine that they would drink, and gave them vegetables.
Yes, those who eat of his dainties will destroy him, and his army will be swept away. Many will fall down slain.

definitions.full: H6598. path -bag [ מַּתבָּֿג ] (read always [ מַּתְבָּג ]) noun [masculine] portion (of food) for king, delicacies (Persian loanword, compare Sanskrit prati-bhâga , Zend [ pati-baga ; whence] Greek transliteration ποτί-βαζις , Syriac ; Gildem ZKM iv. 213 f. Lag Ges. Abh.73 Bev Dn Dr Dn ); — construct הַמֶּלֶךְ מַּתבַּֿג Dan 1:5 , 8 , 13 , 15 , suffix מַּתבָּֿגָם 1:16 , פַתבָּֿגוֺ אֹכְלֵי 11:26 .
